course_title: Critical Writing in Hispanic Topics: Movements in the Americas
subject: SPAN
course_description: This course combines advanced writing instruction with the study of diverse Hispanic cultural topics.
course_notes: This course examines the history and cultures of the Americas through the multiple meanings of the word movement. Movement is not simply the displacement of people from one place to another. It is a force through which worlds are made, transformed, connected, and contested. Geographies are never entirely fixed: they are shaped by migration, contagion, paths, encounters, trade, extraction, and, often, by gatekeepers who try to control movement. We will therefore study not only how humans move and make places through migration and dwelling, but also how things such as potatoes, corn, petroleum, sugar cane, bananas, cows, pigs, grasses, and mosquitoes have traveled and helped define the Americas. For this purpose, this course surveys essential texts and cultural artifacts in Hispanic Studies to trace how ideas, scientific knowledge, languages, labor, money, dictatorships, revolutions, protests, and empires move across geographical and temporal boundaries. The course is ultimately an invitation to learn how to perceive movement and to ask what happens when people, things, organisms, ideas, and capital move. By following these movements, students will connect different geographies and historical periods while developing critical writing skills and new ways of reading the Americas. Prerequisite: SPAN 212 or an Official Spanish Placement into our Foundational Course level. Take the online Spanish Placement Exam at http://spanport.emory.edu/home/undergraduate/placement/index.html.
